sections.h2: Groundwater schemes make up 94.8% of India's 23.14 million minor irrigation schemes

chart.title: Groundwater, not canals, accounts for nearly all counted schemes
chart.sub: Share of all minor irrigation schemes, %, reference year 2017-18.
chart.source: 6th Minor Irrigation Census, Ministry of Jal Shakti, 2017-18.

sections.means: Groundwater borewells and tubewells make up 21.93 million of the 23.14 million schemes counted.
sections.todo: Start irrigation policy discussion from the groundwater scheme count rather than only canal and dam networks.

sections.h2: 96.6% of all schemes are privately owned, including 98.3% of groundwater schemes

chart.title: Surface-water schemes are less often private than groundwater ones
chart.sub: Share of each scheme type that is privately owned, %.
chart.source: 6th Minor Irrigation Census, Ministry of Jal Shakti, 2017-18.

sections.means: Private ownership is near-universal for groundwater schemes at 98.3%, and lower at 64.2% for surface-water schemes.
sections.todo: Treat privately owned, self-built groundwater infrastructure as the core of the irrigation system when assessing investment.

sections.h2: Groundwater schemes grew 6.9% since the fifth census, surface water only 1.2%

chart.title: Groundwater schemes expanded far faster than surface-water ones
chart.source: 6th Minor Irrigation Census, Ministry of Jal Shakti, 2017-18.

sections.means: Growth since the previous census has come mostly from groundwater schemes, up 6.9% against 1.2% for surface water.
sections.todo: Direct irrigation investment attention to the groundwater side, where the expansion is happening.
